summary.text: Darren Soto is the Democratic incumbent seeking re-election to Florida's 9th Congressional District. An attorney from Kissimmee, he served in the Florida House and Senate before his election to Congress in 2016, and now serves on the House Energy and Commerce Committee.

paragraphs.text: Soto was born in Ringwood, New Jersey, to a Puerto Rican father and an Italian-American mother, and attended Lakeland Regional High School.
He graduated from Rutgers College in 2000 with a B.A. in economics and earned a law degree from George Washington University in 2004.
He moved to Florida in 2002 while in law school and was admitted to the Florida Bar in 2005, and he practiced commercial, real estate, family and civil rights law.
Before entering politics he worked as president of D. Soto Law Offices and as a financial analyst with Prudential Insurance.
Soto was first elected to the Florida House of Representatives in a 2007 special election and served there until 2012, then served in the Florida Senate from 2012 to 2016.
In 2016 he was elected to the U.S. House; his office describes him as the first congressman of Puerto Rican descent elected to represent Florida.

He is assigned to the House Energy and Commerce Committee, where his 2025-2026 subcommittee assignment is Commerce, Manufacturing, and Trade, and he has also served on the Natural Resources and Agriculture committees.

According to his official bio, his H.R. 4528, closing a loophole in the Billfish Conservation Act, was signed into law on August 2, 2018, and his H.R. 4042, renaming a Kissimmee post office for the Borinqueneers, was signed into law on March 23, 2018.
